title: Deployable rerank blueprint for crosslingual minibatch fallbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our current reranking endpoint uses a single cross-encoder family for high-quality pairwise scoring. This leads to two pain points: (1) tail latency spikes on long sequences and large batch windows in global regions, and (2) quality regressions for lower-resource languages when we switch quantized variants or compact architectures. Goal: Produce a deployable engineering blueprint that enables: (a) deterministic model selection per-request (quality-first vs latency-first), (b) crosslingual minibatch fallback flow that routes difficult locales to higher-precision variants, and (c) an automated regression harness keyed by locale/prompt-set that prevents silent quality drops during upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated model-selection policy implemented in the rerank router that selects model variant based on request metadata (locale, desired latency bucket, token-length).
implementation_notes:
- Expose selection signals in the request envelope (locale, expected token count, client latency preference).
- Implement a lightweight gating service (stateless) that returns model_variant and batch_hint.
- Add a minibatch fallback mode: if primary variant would exceed per-request latency SLO given current queue depth, route to compact high-precision fallback or use prefix-KV warmstart.
- Maintain compatibility with existing rollout API (canary/A-B) and support rollbacks.
- Ensure the selection path adds <100us p95 to routing latency.
- Instrumentation hooks: selected_variant, queue_depth_at_dispatch, estimated_cost, downstream_latency.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): validate selection heuristics on synthetic traffic and existing traffic shadowing (1 week). Phase 2 (canary): 5% traffic with locale-stratified sampling and active quality evaluation (2 weeks). Phase 3 (ramped): 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated regression gates; abort on metric degradation or p99 latency breach.
Fallback behavior: default to the current stable cross-encoder when selection service is unavailable.
Rollback: immediate traffic switch using existing rollout API.
smoke_tests:
- End-to-end rerank call with english, spanish, hindi locales and token lengths [32, 512, 2048].
- Verify routing header includes variant and batch_hint.
- Assert p95 end-to-end latency under 120ms for latency-first requests in us-east region.
- Validate that multilingual quality checks (BLEU-ish pairwise A/B on curated sets) do not regress beyond configured threshold (delta < 0.8%).
metrics: Primary: locale-weighted pairwise accuracy (holdout prompt sets), p95 end-to-end latency, p99 latency, tokens/sec throughput, per-request cost. Secondary: selection-error-rate, fallback-activation-rate, rollback-rate.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: false negatives in selection heuristics leading to user-visible latency. Mitigation: conservative thresholds in canary, realtime rollback triggers and shadowing for 48h before canary.
Risk: hidden quality regressions for low-resource locales. Mitigation: add per-locale regression tests and require zero-regression gate for locales above traffic threshold.
Risk: increased operational complexity. Mitigation: keep selection service minimal and document runbook + observability dashboard.
